messages:
alex_k: FYI — saw a p99 spike (~18%) on the INT8 dedicated canary after the kernel-selector tweak. Long-context jobs (ded-dev-3) show KV cache memory growing over time instead of stabilizing. Repro profile uploaded to perf bucket.

maria_chen: Can you drop the flamegraph/snippets here? :eyes:

alex_k: pasted the hot paths from the trace (trimmed):
```
hot functions:
  34.2% memcpy (kv_page_copy)
  21.1% attention::matmul_generic
  15.6% kernel_selector::choose_kernel
  9.8% kv_cache::write_page
  6.3% alloc::grow
notes: kernel_selector switched fused_int8_v1 -> matmul_generic for sequences > 1024
```

riley: matmul_generic isn't INT8 packed — it unpacks into FP32/BF16 temporaries then repacks. That explains both extra mem churn and extra copies during page writes + eviction.

sanjay_p: I ran a microbench (longctx ~ 65k tokens, int8, residency=0.7): int8 mem delta +14% over 30m, BF16 run flat. Also saw kv_page_copies steadily increase.

perfbot: perfbot: uploaded full trace -> s3://redwood-perf/canaries/2141598723/trace.json ; p99 baseline 760ms -> 900ms (post-change) ; kv_page_copies/sec +3.4x

maria_chen: Two main hypotheses: 1) kernel selector heuristic is choosing a slower generic kernel for certain seq-len buckets, causing unpack/repack; 2) the eviction/reuse logic expects an on-disk/layout-compatible page format — INT8 packed layout differs so warmup misses and we end up copying/transforming pages on every reuse.

alex_k: quick config excerpt from the canary that reproduced: 
```json
{"kv.cache.eviction_policy":"strided-evict","kv.cache.residency_watermark":"0.8","kv.cache.prefetch_warmup":"true","model.quant.layout":"per_channel_int8","kernel_selector.longseq_threshold":"1024"}
```
Can we try toggling prefetch_warmup -> false and/or pin kernel_selector to fused_int8_v1 for the canary?

riley: forced kernel pin to fused_int8_v1 in ded-dev-3: p99 dropped to ~720ms and memory stabilized. So root cause looks like the selector bump.

sanjay_p: Suggested action items:
- revert the kernel-selector change for int8 longctx canary (fast rollback).
- add a compatibility check in kv_cache: page_layout_version + quant_layout must match or we avoid on-the-fly repacking.
- add metrics: kv_page_reuses, kv_page_repacks, kv_page_copies to console and alerts if repacks > 1% of writes.
- integration test: long-context end-to-end with int8/bf16 variants for 1hr smoke to catch mem drift.

maria_chen: also suggests we explore hybrid approach: keep per-channel INT8 for most layers but keep attention weights BF16 (critical for reuse layout stability). That buys most mem savings while avoiding page-format churn.

alex_k: I'll open the rollback PR and a follow-up to add the kv page-layout compatibility gate. Canaries: ded-canary-2141598723.

sanjay_p: opening PRs now. I'll attach the microbench script and raw traces.

riley: SGTM. once PRs are out we'll run a focussed canary and watch kv_page_repacks metric. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: scheduled rollback deploy (ded-canary-2141598723) -> 2141599800.

perfbot: perfbot: after forced rollback (pinned kernel) quick check: p99 -> 730ms; memory growth stops. Full regression test queued.

sanjay_p: follow-up TODOs listed in the PR: add unit for page-layout hash, add per-layer quant config, update kernel_selector docs.

alex_k: thanks everyone — copying results into the incident doc and will coordinate the longer-term hybrid quant plan.
